tldr: Kimi K3.1 surfaced as an unreleased name after Arena testing, then Moonshot launched the roughly 3T-parameter K3.1 Pro on Oct 24. A quota-driven rocky rollout was followed by third-party hosting, vLLM day-0 support and, on Nov 5, full open weights.
whats_new: Huawei Ascend adapted Kimi K3.1 Pro for LoRA fine-tuning on a 128-card Atlas 950 SuperPoD on Nov 8, a day after Moore Threads added day-zero inference support.
why_it_matters: K3.1 Pro is now self-hostable on vLLM, Ascend and MTT S5000, and vLLM's RL work shows it is also a fine-tuning target. Licence terms and a 1.56TB footprint decide whether that beats third-party hosts or first-party quotas.

status.detail: K3.1 Pro moved from a quota-troubled first-party launch to third-party hosting, vLLM support, full open weights and now a second Chinese accelerator (Moore Threads) beyond Huawei Ascend. Independent quality and cost data are still thin.

beats.headline: Kimi K3.1 surfaces after Arena testing
beats.summary: Coverage names the unreleased model and signals an imminent release.

beats.headline: K3.1 Pro set against Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra
beats.summary: R&D World frames a head-to-head; only the headline is in the item, so results are unconfirmed here.

beats.headline: Moonshot launches K3.1 Pro, a roughly 3T-parameter flagship
beats.summary: SiliconANGLE reports the launch; Latent Space calls it near closed-model quality with open weights and notes a faster Highspeed API tier.

beats.headline: Quotas reset after user complaints; Moonshot apologises
beats.summary: Users hit quota problems after launch; Moonshot reset the quotas on Oct 26 and apologised and restored them on Oct 27.

beats.headline: NEAR and ZenMux add K3.1 Pro
beats.summary: Third-party platforms list the model, ZenMux for long-context workflows.

beats.headline: vLLM day-0 support and Verda preview
beats.summary: vLLM details sparse attention on a KDA hybrid, a packed KV cache and fused low-latency decode; Verda previews inference with K3.1 Pro.

beats.headline: Full weights published, Huawei Ascend adds day-zero support
beats.summary: Moonshot releases the full 1.56TB, 2.8T-parameter weights with conditional commercial use; Huawei Ascend lists day-zero support.

beats.headline: Moore Threads adds day-zero K3.1 Pro support on MTT S5000 GPUs
beats.summary: A second Chinese accelerator vendor follows Huawei Ascend, two days after the weights shipped.

beats.headline: vLLM applies zero-mismatch async RL to Kimi K3.1
beats.summary: vLLM describes aligning rollout and training kernels and unclipped importance sampling for stale-weight lag, covering DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Kimi K3.1 and AMD MI355X.

open_questions: Do independent evals show K3.1 Pro matching Opus 5.5 on coding or agent tasks?
What do the commercial-use conditions in the weights licence actually restrict?
What do third-party hosts charge versus Moonshot's first-party plans and quotas?
Does anyone publish a K3.1 RL fine-tune that uses vLLM's zero-mismatch setup?
Do Ascend and MTT S5000 deployments match vLLM-on-NVIDIA quality and throughput for K3.1 Pro?
take_for_builders: Read the weights licence conditions before planning a self-host, and budget for 1.56TB of storage. Pin the vLLM version and rerun your own evals against Opus 5.5 before changing routing; for RL, check the bit-for-bit kernel alignment in vLLM's post first.
